newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended unchanged to about 1/8 point higher after slightly more promising morning gains ebbed in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries.
"We were a little bit firmer this morning, we lost it with the Treasuries," a municipal analyst said.

High-grade issues ended flat to slightly improved, while dollar bonds largely mirrored the broader market. Early session activity was light to moderate, with little action seen heading into the close.
A municipal trader described the market as mixed, with prices up 1/4 point or down that much depending on the issue.
"(Prices) wanted to do better, and they did for a while today, but now we're kind of getting full again," he said.
Thursday's 1-1/2 point rise by 30-year U.S. Treasuries helped lift municipals during that session, and prices opened stronger Friday, the trader said.

"I would say we were up a solid nickel from yesterday, and then it seemed like we wanted to do a little bit better," he said. "A few things traded and then we kind of backed off a couple of basis points."
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was nearing the close down 5/32 at 98-23/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed up 8/32 at 116-9/32. The March T-bond contract closed up 5/32 at 113-10/32. The MOB spread was 95 ticks.
In new issues, the New York State Environmental Facilities Corp tentatively priced $63.5 million bonds at a 5.65 percent top yield in 2016.

The deal had been expected next week. Without it, competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for the week of December 23 are now expected to total a mere $20 million in five offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Three competitive sales are expected, totaling $5.6 million. The largest issue is a $2.9 million Janesville, Wis., issue on December 23 at 1200 EST.
Negotiated sales are expected total $15 million in two offerings.
